questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How engineers build a chatbot at Google
Hollywood films about robots taking over
Whether AI can really think or be conscious
Why software engineers lose their jobs
questions.why: Neil says they'll discuss whether artificial intelligence is capable of consciousness.

questions.q: What did Blake Lemoine conclude after months of talking to LaMDA?
options: It was just a simple machine with no mind
It was a person with wishes and rights
It was dangerous and should be switched off
It could not understand films or books
questions.why: He concluded the chatbot was an intelligent person with wishes and rights that should be respected.

questions.q: How did Google react to Blake's ideas?
options: It moved him, saying evidence didn't support him
It promoted him to lead a new AI team
It agreed publicly that LaMDA was a person
It made LaMDA an official employee
questions.why: Google reassigned Blake, announcing his ideas were not supported by the evidence.

questions.q: Why does Professor Emily Bender dislike the phrase 'speech recognition'?
options: It is too long
It is too technical for most people
It is an old-fashioned term
It suggests the computer is thinking
questions.why: She says 'recognition' suggests something cognitive is going on.

questions.q: What term does Professor Bender suggest instead?
options: Machine learning
Automatic transcription
Speech understanding
Computer listening
questions.why: She says a better term would be automatic transcription.

questions.q: What happens when people meet natural-sounding language from a computer?
options: They immediately know it's a machine
They stop trusting it
They can't help imagining a mind behind it
They find it boring
questions.why: Sam says humans can't help but imagine a mind behind the language, even when there isn't one.

questions.q: Why does Professor Bender mention dolls and companies?
options: To show we see human qualities in things
To explain how AI is advertised and sold
To compare children's toys with computers
To show that companies build dolls with AI
questions.why: She says we anthropomorphise action figures, dolls and companies, seeing ourselves in the world around us.

questions.q: According to Professor Bender, when are people more likely to be tricked?
options: When the text is short and simple
When the computer makes mistakes
When they are using AI for the first time
When the text is fluent and covers many topics
questions.why: She says the more fluent the text and the more topics, the more chances to get taken in.
